lines.trans: You took your time—did the boss try his famous alley shortcut past the kitchen?
Never mind the route, Mazen! What is that yellow envelope in your hand?!
Express station post, signed for at eleven-forty while you were chasing clock shadows.
Look at the sender line on the left—it is from our Room Eight mapmaker!
Open it, Nour, open it before my glasses fall right off my nose!
Arriving in Amman next Saturday for the thirtieth May anniversary at Jasmine Courtyard!
Next Saturday?! The original guest from Room Eight is coming HERE in person?!
Read the last line at the bottom—that is the part for the kitchen.
Hoping with all my heart to taste one slice of that famous berry almond cake!
Merciful heavens, we still only have the TOP HALF of that cake recipe!
Better go ask Suad about that old green garden book in Room Four right now.
Up the stairs we go—next Saturday is seven days away, and the oven awaits!

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: The word 'جرب' (jarrab) means 'he tried'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طولتوا—المدير جرب اختصاره المشهور بالزقاق اللي مارق من المطبخ؟
examples.trans: You took your time—did the boss try his famous alley shortcut past the kitchen?
This is جرب.

meanings.note: The word 'اختصار' (ikhtiSaar) means 'shortcut'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تلات بلوكات لفوق بالشارع الرئيسي؟ حكي فاضي، أنا بعرف اختصار بدقيقتين!
examples.trans: Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!
This is اختصار.

meanings.note: البنت المشهورة describes Layan's high-profile popularity across school.

examples.trans: Layan is well-known across the whole school.
This is a famous restaurant in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزقة.

examples.trans: The stone alley is narrow and quiet.
We turned past the narrow lane.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: The word 'مارق' (maareq) means 'passing'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طولتوا—المدير جرب اختصاره المشهور بالزقاق اللي مارق من المطبخ؟
examples.trans: You took your time—did the boss try his famous alley shortcut past the kitchen?
This is مارق.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسى, بينسى).

examples.trans: You forgot the notebook beside the soup bowl.
With all the rush, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Used in عالطريق ('on the way') and طول الطريق ('all the way').

examples.trans: The hot tea is on the way right now!
I repeated the sentence all along the way.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: The word 'مازن' (مازن) means 'مازن'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صارت الضهر تقريبا! خلينا نسأل مازن إذا وصل أي طرود.
examples.trans: It is almost noon! Let us ask Mazen if any packages arrived.
This is مازن.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مغلفات.

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the door.
We opened the thick envelope calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A postcard arrived in the morning.
The postman rang the bell.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: The word 'إحدعش' (iHda3sh) means 'eleven'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بريد سريع من المحطة، وقعت عليه الساعة إحدعش وأربعين دقيقة وانتو بتلحقوا خيالات الساعة.
examples.trans: Express station post, signed for at eleven-forty while you were chasing clock shadows.
This is إحدعش.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: The word 'انتو' (w-intoo) means 'and you all'. It is a common pron in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بريد سريع من المحطة، وقعت عليه الساعة إحدعش وأربعين دقيقة وانتو بتلحقوا خيالات الساعة.
examples.trans: Express station post, signed for at eleven-forty while you were chasing clock shadows.
This is انتو.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلحق, بيلحق).

examples.trans: Follow me quickly to the third floor!

examples.text: لحقنا دكان الخردوات أول ما فتح.
examples.trans: We caught the hardware shop right as it opened.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian speech, خيال commonly means a cast 'shadow' or 'silhouette' as well as 'imagination'.

examples.text: شفت خيال القطة على الحيط تحت الفانوس.
examples.trans: I saw the cat's shadow on the wall beneath the lantern.

examples.text: خيال الشجرة واصل لحد باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: The tree's shadow reaches right to the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطور.

examples.trans: Read me the top line of the letter.
He wrote two short lines on the card.

meanings.note: The word 'مرسل' (mursil) means 'sender'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ساعي البريد تركه قبل ساعة؛ ما في عنوان مرسل.
examples.trans: The postman left that an hour ago; there is no return address.
This is مرسل.

meanings.note: The word 'يسار' (yasaar) means 'left'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يسار بعد قواوير الورد، ويسار كمان مرة بعد السور الأخضر—لوين رايحين؟!
examples.trans: Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!
This is يسار.

meanings.note: The word 'رسام' (rassaam) means 'mapmaker'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ليش رسام الخرايط رسم نجمة حمرا على بلكونة ساحتنا اللي فوق؟!
examples.trans: Why did the mapmaker paint a red star on our upstairs courtyard balcony?!
This is رسام.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خرايط.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: The word 'تمنية' (tmanye) means 'eight'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا سطر المرسل عاليسار—هادا من رسام الخرايط تبع غرفة تمنية!
examples.trans: Look at the sender line on the left—it is from our Room Eight mapmaker!
This is تمنية.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: The word 'منخار' (munkhaari) means 'my nose'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: افتحيه يا نور، افتحيه قبل ما نظاراتي يوقعوا عن منخاري!
examples.trans: Open it, Nour, open it before my glasses fall right off my nose!
This is منخار.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واصلة, plural: واصلين).

examples.text: ريحة القرفة الدافية واصلة للطابق التاني!
examples.trans: The warm cinnamon scent reaches all the way to the second floor!
The bus is pulling into the station now.

meanings.note: The word 'عمان' (عمان) means 'عمان'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: واصل على عمان السبت الجاي لذكرى شهر خمسة التلاتين بـ بيت الياسمين!
examples.trans: Arriving in Amman next Saturday for the thirtieth May anniversary at Jasmine Courtyard!
This is عمان.

meanings.note: The word 'سبت' (el-sabt) means 'Saturday'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو هالصباح الحلو يوم السبت لمشية كنز بشارع شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
This is سبت.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ذكريات.

examples.trans: This house is full of sweet memories.
Childhood memories are never forgotten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شهور.

examples.trans: That was the best sleep in a month!
The contract renews at the start of next month.

meanings.note: Numeral 'five'; short form خمس (khams) before a plural noun (خمس دقايق 'five minutes').

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: The word 'بـ' (b-) means 'in'. It is a common prep in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: احنا بدينا بـ بيت الياسمين! لازم نمشي كل هالطريق نرجع؟!
examples.trans: We started at Jasmine Courtyard! Do we have to walk all the way back?!
This is بـ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: The word 'الياسمين' (الياسمين) means 'الياسمين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو هالصباح الحلو يوم السبت لمشية كنز بشارع شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
This is الياسمين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أصلية, plural: أصليين).

examples.trans: The ceiling is solid oak wood.
All the old tilework is original.

meanings.note: The word 'لهون' (lahoon) means 'to here'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مربع صغير من ورق الألوان المائية! هاتيه لهون بسرعة!
examples.trans: A small square of watercolour paper! Hand it here quickly!
This is لهون.

meanings.note: The word 'شخصيا' (shakhSiyyan) means 'in person'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: السبت الجاي؟! الضيف الأصلي تبع غرفة تمنية جاي لهون شخصيا؟!
examples.trans: Next Saturday?! The original guest from Room Eight is coming HERE in person?!
This is شخصيا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Names the heel of a foot or shoe (كعب القدم / كعب الحذاء).

examples.text: زحلق كعب حذائي عن حرف الطبلية الواطية.
examples.trans: The heel of my shoe slipped off the edge of the low stool.

examples.text: اسندي كعبك عالوسادة الطرية عشان ترتاح رجلك.
examples.trans: Rest your heel on the soft cushion so your foot can relax.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجزاء.

examples.trans: This is the sweetest part of the story.
I read the first part of the book.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb without أن in spoken Arabic (بتتمنى تكون 'wishes to be').

examples.trans: I hope we'll be in the same class.
Every girl wishes to succeed.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قلوب.

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast with joy!
Welcome from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: The word 'ذاق' (adooq) means 'I taste'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بتمنى من كل قلبي أدوق شقفة واحدة من كيكة اللوز والتوت المشهورة!
examples.trans: Hoping with all my heart to taste one slice of that famous berry almond cake!
This is ذاق.

meanings.note: The word 'شقفة' (shuqfe) means 'slice/piece'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بتمنى من كل قلبي أدوق شقفة واحدة من كيكة اللوز والتوت المشهورة!
examples.trans: Hoping with all my heart to taste one slice of that famous berry almond cake!
This is شقفة.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كيكات.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Collective noun for almonds (singulative لوزة).

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: The word 'توت' (wel-toot) means 'and berries'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: نعلق فوانيس من بلكونة النجمة الحمرا ونشارك كيكة اللوز والتوت كمان مرة!
examples.trans: To hang lanterns from the red-star balcony and share berry almond cake again!
This is توت.

meanings.note: The word 'رحمة' (raHmetak) means 'your mercy'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يا رحمتك يا رب، احنا لسه معنا بس النص الفوقاني تبع هالوصفة!
examples.trans: Merciful heavens, we still only have the TOP HALF of that cake recipe!
This is رحمة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرباب.

examples.trans: Oh goodness, help us today!
Praise be to the Lord of all worlds.

meanings.note: The word 'احنا' (iHna) means 'we'. It is a common pron in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أها! شوفوا هالحيط التاريخي الهادي—أكيد احنا بالزبط ورا ساحة الساعة!
examples.trans: Aha! Behold this quiet historic wall—we must be right behind the clock square!
This is احنا.

meanings.note: The word 'لسه' (lissa) means 'still'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بعد تلاتين سنة، طيور الصبح لسه محافظين على موعدهم!
examples.trans: Thirty years later, the morning birds are still keeping their appointment!
This is لسه.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فوقانية, plural: فوقانيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
The red ribbon is in the top pocket.

meanings.note: The word 'وصفة' (hal-waSfe) means 'this recipe'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يا رحمتك يا رب، احنا لسه معنا بس النص الفوقاني تبع هالوصفة!
examples.trans: Merciful heavens, we still only have the TOP HALF of that cake recipe!
This is وصفة.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of منيح ('good'). Before a noun without ال- it means 'the best' (أحسن نومة 'the best sleep').

examples.trans: This is the best room in the house.
I feel better today.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

راح.gloss: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)

meanings.en: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بروح, بيروح).

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسأل, بيسأل).

examples.trans: Ask him what his name is on the phone!
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: The word 'سعاد' (سعاد) means 'سعاد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أحسن إشي تروحوا تسألوا سعاد عن كتاب الجنينة الأخضر القديم بغرفة أربعة هلق.
examples.trans: Better go ask Suad about that old green garden book in Room Four right now.
This is سعاد.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a garden or yard; a small one is a جنينة, the formal word is حديقة.

examples.trans: We have a small garden behind the house.
The children are playing in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The word 'هلق' (hallaq) means 'now'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هلق شوفوا منيح عالكرت الأول عشان نشوف شو الرمز اللي لازم نلاقيه.
examples.trans: Now look closely at Card One to see what symbol we need to find.
This is هلق.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Active participle of ضل ('to remain'); standard Jordanian for 'there is ... left'.

examples.trans: He has two valves left on the shelf.
How much time is left until noon?

meanings.note: The word 'لـ' (لـ) means 'لـ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معها حق—أنا عم أعمل لفائف القرفة لفترة بعد الظهر لـ بيت الياسمين.
examples.trans: She is right—I am making the afternoon cinnamon rolls for Jasmine Courtyard.
This is لـ.

meanings.note: The word 'سبع' (saba3) means 'seven'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طالعين عالدرج—السبت الجاي ضايل له سبع أيام، والفرن بيستنى!
examples.trans: Up the stairs we go—next Saturday is seven days away, and the oven awaits!
This is سبع.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.
